page: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. It delivers 1024.0 GB of memory, representing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage includes 7560 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, while discrete GPU acceleration is not provided. Architectural flags confirm support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions.

Benchmark evaluations position this configuration in the top tier for parallel compute, memory throughput, and database execution. It records top-decile multi-core scores in both stress-ng and PassMark suites, accompanied by over 209 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Memory throughput is substantial, measuring 655.3 GB/s for large-block uncached reads and 253.51 GB/s for writes. Multi-threaded compression operations mirror this performance. In contrast, single-core compute and LLM token generation metrics operate within average benchmark ranges.

The dense memory-to-core allocation paired with broad internal NVMe storage provides strong qualitative resource efficiency by consolidating memory-heavy architectures onto a single node without external storage overhead. The configuration exhibits a tradeoff between average single-threaded execution speed and high parallel capacity. Appropriate deployment workloads include distributed caching layers, in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, and analytical ETL processing pipelines.
